trigger: HER2-EXP-003: Reactome confirms PI3K-GSK3β-NRF2-SLC7A11 chain; SLC7A11 paradox resolved
claim: T-DXd kills trastuzumab-resistant HER2+ BC via a double-hit ferroptosis mechanism that specifically exploits the SLC7A11-high escape phenotype: (1) ANTIBODY HIT — trastuzumab component reactivates GSK3β (via PI3K/AKT suppression) → NRF2 degradation (BTRC:CUL1, Reactome R-HSA-9762114) → SLC7A11 transcription falls, removing GSH synthesis capacity; (2) PAYLOAD HIT — DXd → TOP1mt → VDAC3-HSPB1 mitochondrial ferroptosis (PMID 39243601) that BYPASSES cytosolic GPX4/SLC7A11 protection. Trastuzumab-resistant tumors with epigenetically upregulated SLC7A11 (H3K4me3, PMID 40464376) are specifically vulnerable because the same NRF2-SLC7A11 axis that enabled trastuzumab escape is dismantled by T-DXd's antibody component. Biomarker: SLC7A11 IHC H-score + NRF2 nuclear IHC in trastuzumab-pretreated HER2+ tumor banks.
paradox_resolution: SLC7A11 is anti-ferroptotic (cytosolic cystine import → GSH → GPX4). The apparent paradox (SLC7A11-high = resistant, yet we claim vulnerability) is resolved: T-DXd's antibody strips cytosolic protection (NRF2 degradation → SLC7A11↓) while the payload delivers mitochondrial ferroptosis that GPX4/SLC7A11 cannot rescue. The two mechanisms are orthogonal — neither alone is sufficient in SLC7A11-high cells, but together they overcome resistance.

evidence.finding: T-DXd induces ferroptosis via crVDAC3-HSPB1 mitochondrial axis in HER2-low BC
SLC7A11 epigenetically upregulated (H3K4me3 + DNA hypomethylation) in trastuzumab-resistant HER2+ BC
GSK3B phosphorylates NRF2 → BTRC:CUL1 ubiquitination → NRF2 degraded. PI3K/AKT inhibition (by trastuzumab) reactivates GSK3B.
AcK-NFE2L2 and ATF4 cooperatively bind and activate SLC7A11 gene transcription. NRF2 degradation → SLC7A11 transcription falls.
NRF2 is the master transcription factor for SLC7A11
SLC7A11 CV=59.4% in HER2-enriched subtype (n=78), supporting IHC stratification

novelty.note: Double-hit mechanism exploiting antibody/payload synergy for ferroptosis is entirely novel; no published proposal
